title: Earth, Sun & Moon
description: Grade 4 Science: the Earth, Sun and Moon — day and night, the Sun as our star, the Moon's phases, and the solar system. Label the day-night diagram and order the moon phases.

topics.title: Our Home, the Earth
topics.concept:
The Earth is the planet we live on. It is just right for life:

  • 💧 It has plenty of water — oceans, rivers and rain.
  • 🌬️ It has air for living things to breathe.
  • 🌡️ It is the perfect distance from the Sun — not too hot, not too cold.

The Earth is shaped like a giant ball (a sphere). From space it looks blue and green because of its water and land.

recap: Earth is the planet we live on, shaped like a ball.
It has water, air and the right warmth for life.
From space, Earth looks blue and green.

wonder.text: Out of all the worlds in space, only one is known to have living things. What makes Earth so special?

qa.q: Why is Earth called the 'blue planet'?
qa.a: Because so much of Earth is covered in water — the oceans. From space, all that water makes the Earth look mostly blue, with green and brown land and white clouds.

qa.q: Why can we live on Earth but not on the Moon?
qa.a: Earth has air to breathe, water to drink and the right warmth. The Moon has no air or liquid water, so living things cannot survive there.

topics.title: Day and Night
topics.concept:
The Earth is always spinning like a top. This spinning is called rotation, and it causes day and night.

  • ☀️ The side of Earth facing the Sun has day.
  • 🌙 The side facing away from the Sun has night.
  • 🔄 Earth takes 24 hours (one day) to spin around once.

So the Sun does not really move across the sky — WE are moving, as the Earth turns!

recap: Earth spins (rotates), causing day and night.
The side facing the Sun has day; the other side has night.
Earth takes 24 hours to spin around once.

wonder.text: The Sun seems to rise, cross the sky and set. But is it really the Sun that moves?

qa.q: If Earth is spinning, why don't we feel it?
qa.a: Earth spins very smoothly and we move along with it, so we cannot feel it — just like you don't feel a smooth train moving if you close your eyes.

qa.q: Is it day everywhere at the same time?
qa.a: No! When it is day on our side of Earth, it is night on the opposite side. As Earth spins, day and night travel around the world.

topics.title: The Sun, Our Star
topics.concept:
The Sun is a star — a giant ball of glowing hot gas. It only looks small because it is very, very far away.

  • ☀️ The Sun gives Earth light and heat.
  • 🌍 The Earth and other planets travel around the Sun.
  • ⭐ The twinkling stars at night are other suns, even farther away.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 170" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="170" fill="#0b1437"/><circle cx="80" cy="85" r="38" fill="#FFC93C"/><g stroke="#FFD24D" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"><line x1="80" y1="38" x2="80" y2="26"/><line x1="80" y1="132" x2="80" y2="144"/><line x1="33" y1="85" x2="21" y2="85"/></g><text x="80" y="90" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#7a4a00" text-anchor="middle">Sun</text><g fill="#ffe98a"><circle cx="210" cy="50" r="3"/><circle cx="250" cy="80" r="3"/><circle cx="225" cy="110" r="3"/><circle cx="265" cy="130" r="2.5"/></g><text x="235" y="160" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#cfd6ff" text-anchor="middle">Stars are far-off suns</text></svg>
recap: The Sun is a star — a huge ball of hot, glowing gas.
It gives Earth light and heat.
Night-time stars are other suns, much farther away.

wonder.text: The Sun looks small in the sky, but it is so huge that over a million Earths could fit inside it. What exactly is the Sun?

qa.a: Yes! The Sun is a star, just like the ones that twinkle at night. It looks much bigger and brighter only because it is the closest star to us.

qa.q: Why do other stars look so tiny?
qa.a: Other stars are suns too, but they are millions of times farther away than our Sun. That huge distance makes them look like tiny twinkling dots.

topics.title: The Moon and Its Phases
topics.concept:
The Moon is Earth's neighbour in space. It travels around the Earth and does not make its own light — it reflects the Sun's light.

As the Moon moves around Earth, we see different amounts of its lit side. These shapes are called phases:

  • 🌑 New Moon — we see no Moon.
  • 🌒 Crescent — a thin sliver.
  • 🌓 Half Moon — half lit.
  • 🌕 Full Moon — a bright full circle.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 130" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="340" height="130" fill="#0b1437"/><text x="40" y="64" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🌑</text><text x="105" y="64" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🌒</text><text x="170" y="64" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🌓</text><text x="235" y="64" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🌔</text><text x="300" y="64" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🌕</text><text x="170" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#cfd6ff" text-anchor="middle">The phases of the Moon</text></svg>
recap: The Moon travels around Earth and reflects sunlight.
We see phases: new, crescent, half and full Moon.
The Moon is always round — only the lit part we see changes.

wonder.text: Some nights the Moon is a full circle, other nights just a thin sliver. Why does the Moon keep changing shape?

qa.q: Does the Moon really change shape?
qa.a: No — the Moon is always a round ball! We just see different amounts of its sunlit side as it travels around Earth. The shape we see is called its phase.

qa.q: How long is one full set of Moon phases?
qa.a: About one month! The Moon takes around 29 days to go through all its phases, from new moon back to new moon again.

topics.title: The Solar System
topics.concept:
The Solar System is the Sun and everything that travels around it. This includes eight planets, their moons, and smaller rocks.

  • ☀️ The Sun is at the centre.
  • 🪐 Eight planets orbit it: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
  • 🔄 The path a planet takes around the Sun is called its orbit.
  • 📅 Earth takes one year (about 365 days) to go around the Sun once.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="200" fill="#0b1437"/><g fill="none" stroke="#3a4a7a" stroke-width="1"><ellipse cx="70" cy="100" rx="60" ry="44"/><ellipse cx="70" cy="100" rx="100" ry="74"/><ellipse cx="70" cy="100" rx="140" ry="96"/></g><circle cx="70" cy="100" r="26" fill="#FFC93C"/><circle cx="130" cy="100" r="7" fill="#c98a4a"/><circle cx="170" cy="100" r="9" fill="#3f86d6"/><circle cx="210" cy="100" r="16" fill="#e0a060"/><text x="70" y="106" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#7a4a00" text-anchor="middle">Sun</text><text x="248" y="40" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#cfd6ff" text-anchor="middle">Planets orbit the Sun</text></svg>
recap: The Solar System is the Sun and all that orbits it.
Eight planets orbit the Sun, including Earth.
Earth takes one year to revolve around the Sun once.

wonder.text: Earth is not alone — it has seven planet neighbours, all circling the same Sun. Can you name one?

qa.q: What is the difference between rotation and revolution?
qa.a: Rotation is Earth SPINNING on its own (causing day and night). Revolution is Earth TRAVELLING all the way around the Sun (taking one year). Two different motions!
Jupiter is the biggest planet in our Solar System — so huge that all the other planets could fit inside it! Earth is quite small next to giant Jupiter.

questions.q: The Earth is shaped like a…
questions.explanation: Earth is shaped like a giant ball, called a sphere.

questions.q: Day and night are caused by the Earth's…
questions.explanation: Earth spins on its axis, giving us day and night.
The Sun is a star — a huge ball of hot, glowing gas.
The Moon reflects sunlight; it makes no light of its own.

questions.q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: There are eight planets in our Solar System.
Earth takes about 365 days (one year) to revolve around the Sun.

questions.q: If Earth is spinning, why don't we feel it?
options: It spins smoothly and we move with it
questions.explanation: Earth spins smoothly and we move along with it, so we cannot feel it.

questions.q: What is the difference between rotation and revolution?
options: Rotation is spinning (day/night); revolution is going round the Sun (year)
questions.explanation: Rotation is Earth spinning; revolution is Earth orbiting the Sun.

questions.q: Why does the Moon look like it changes shape?
options: We see different amounts of its sunlit side as it orbits Earth
questions.explanation: The Moon is always round; we just see different amounts of its lit side — its phases.

questions.q: Why do other stars look tiny while the Sun looks big?
options: The Sun is bigger than all stars
Other stars are millions of times farther away
The Sun is closer to the Moon
questions.explanation: Other stars are suns too, but very far away, so they look like tiny dots.

questions.q: Order the Moon phases: full, new, half, crescent (from no Moon).
questions.explanation: From no Moon: new → crescent → half → full.
